input: Over the course of one quarter, a defect-reduction project on a packing line succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 3.6% to 2.1%, which represents a substantial improvement in the performance of the line. At a throughput of 259k units per year, this change avoids approximately 3885 rejected units per year, which is a considerable saving in wasted product and rework. It should be noted, however, that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates have not been adjusted to allow for it, so the comparison effectively runs between a quarter containing a shutdown and the period that came before it, on the basis of the rates exactly as recorded. The reduction is nonetheless clearly visible in the recorded rates, and the avoided-units figure follows directly from those rates at the stated annual volume. The project concentrated on the causes that the line records had already separated out, namely misfeeds at the infeed, seal faults that presented themselves as weight rejects, and label faults at the printer. Each cause was addressed in turn, the countermeasures were fitted during planned stops, and the reject count was read from the same checkweigher record before and after, which means that the rate comparison rests on a single instrument and a single counting rule throughout. A later quarter without a shutdown will provide a comparison over a full running period, and the project will be judged once again on that quarter before the change is adopted as settled practice on the line.
target: A defect-reduction project on a packing line cut the reject rate from 3.6% to 2.1% over one quarter. At 259k units per year, the change avoids about 3885 rejected units per year. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it; the comparison therefore runs between a quarter with a shutdown in it and the period before it, on the rates as recorded. The reduction stands in the recorded rates, and the avoided-units figure follows from the recorded rates at the stated annual volume. The project worked on the causes the line records had already separated out: misfeeds at the infeed, seal faults that showed as weight rejects, and label faults at the printer. Each cause was taken in turn, the countermeasure was fitted during planned stops, and the reject count was read from the same checkweigher record before and after, so the rate comparison rests on one instrument and one counting rule throughout. A rate read from a changed counting rule would not carry the comparison, and no change of rule was made during the quarter. The avoided units are units that pass the checkweigher instead of leaving the line as waste or rework, and their value to the plant is the product and packing they no longer consume. A later quarter without a shutdown gives the comparison on a full running period, and the project is judged again on that quarter before the change is treated as settled practice on the line.
